item.text:
**Bottom line:** mixed. Sharif showed real internal control in a few core execution areas, especially energy theft, counterterrorism, welfare delivery, and some corrective bureaucratic follow-through. But the record also shows heavy personalization, family/old-guard staffing, weak institutional delegation, and coercive control over media, protest, and courts. That is enough for “some discipline and coordination,” not for a clean finding of strong, durable internal discipline.

**Positive evidence**
- **Education emergency with personal supervision** | Publisher: Radio Pakistan | Date: 2024-05-08 | URL: https://www.radio.gov.pk/08-05-2024/pm-declares-education-emergency-to-enroll-26-million-out-of-school-children | Claim: Sharif set a numeric enrollment target, said he would personally supervise the program, and linked it to provincial coordination and incentives. This is direct evidence of executive follow-through on a flagship priority. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.3
- **Anti-power-theft campaign with task forces** | Publisher: Radio Pakistan | Date: 2024-05-28 | URL: https://www.radio.gov.pk/28-05-2024/shehbaz-sharif-directs-to-minimize-load-shedding | Claim: He ordered monthly reviews, provincial and law-enforcement support, task forces at multiple levels, and expert hiring for DISCO privatization. That is strong evidence of coordinated implementation across bureaucracy and enforcement agencies. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **National counterterrorism campaign** | Publisher: Radio Pakistan | Date: 2024-06-22 | URL: https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism | Claim: Sharif launched a national counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus and explicit resource support for the armed forces. This supports a reading of effective coordination across security forces and provinces. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **BISP digital-wallet delivery reform** | Publisher: APP | Date: 2024-03-18 | URL: https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/ | Claim: Sharif ordered BISP payments onto digital wallets to reduce leakage, delay, and discretion. That is concrete evidence of rule-based implementation rather than ad hoc patronage. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.4
- **Corrective action after FBR failure** | Publisher: Dawn | Date: 2024-05-08 | URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117 | Claim: After an internal report found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective, Sharif ordered action against responsible officials. This shows at least some willingness to correct implementation failures rather than ignore them. | IDs: 8B.5, 7B.10, 8B.4
- **Coalition bargaining held after the hung election** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 2024-02-21 | URL: https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government/1973213/ | Claim: PML-N and PPP reached a formal coalition agreement after a hung parliament. This is weak but real evidence that Sharif could mobilize a ruling bloc and maintain coordination inside a coalition structure. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.1

**Negative evidence**
- **Cabinet still leaned on established political figures** | Publisher: Dawn | Date: 2024-03-01 | URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/1821157 | Claim: Reporting on the new cabinet said it still relied heavily on established political figures. That weakens the case for a clean, capability-driven team and suggests partial rather than strong internal disciplining. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4
- **Family influence in cabinet selection** | Publisher: Dawn | Date: 2024-02-19 | URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/1815365/nawaz-busy-selecting-cabinet-as-khawaja-asif-sees-ppp-n-govt | Claim: Dawn reported Nawaz Sharif was heavily involved behind the scenes in cabinet selection. That is direct counterevidence to fully independent or merit-based staffing. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4
- **Personalized control over ECNEC** | Publisher: Dawn | Date: 2024-06-15 | URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967/pm-shehbaz-relieves-finance-minister-from-key-economic-forum | Claim: Sharif kept direct control over ECNEC rather than fully delegating to the technocrat finance minister. This shows strong central control, but also weak institutional delegation and uneven follow-through. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- **Pressure on media and critics** | Publisher: Human Rights Watch | Date: 2024-01-11 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent | Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, creating self-censorship and fear. That is evidence of control through coercion, not disciplined institutional coordination. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Blocking X around the election period** | Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com | Date: 2024-04-17 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | Claim: The interior ministry confirmed X was blocked on national-security grounds. This shows state control over information channels, but it also indicates a coercive approach to managing scrutiny. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Protest repression and mass arrests** | Publisher: Human Rights Watch | Date: 2024-10-09 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent | Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. That is strong evidence of using security tools for political suppression rather than orderly internal discipline. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Judicial independence weakened** | Publisher: The Guardian | Date: 2024-10-21 | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps | Claim: Critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations. This cuts against the idea that Sharif was building durable, neutral institutions to carry the program forward. | IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4

**Search gap**
- I found solid evidence for targeted executive control in economic and security domains, but not a single source showing a broad, durable system of cross-ministry discipline or routine cabinet-wide monitoring.
- The evidence is mostly episodic: PM directives, reactive inquiries, selective enforcement drives, and coalition bargaining. That is enough to show some coordination, not enough to prove consistently effective whole-of-government discipline.
